name: Barbara Berlusconi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Barbara Berlusconi is the daughter of Silvio Berlusconi, the media mogul and longest-serving Italian prime minister in the post-war era, who died at age 86 in June 2023.
Barbara is one of five heirs to media group Fininvest, which her father started in the late 1970s and built into a national force, importing American shows like 'Baywatch' to Italy.
Her father Silvio, a three-time Italian prime minister, was convicted of tax fraud in 2014 and was initially banned from running for political office until 2019.
She was the CEO of Italian soccer team AC Milan from 2013 to 2017, when her father sold it to Chinese investors for $790 million.
She joined the board of directors of Fininvest in 2003.

name: Max Lytvyn
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Wikidata (2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Max Lytvyn cofounded popular grammar checking tool Grammarly in 2009 with Alex Shevchenko and Dmytro Lider; his current title is head of growth strategy.
The three Ukrainian-born entrepreneurs all worked together on Lytvyn and Shevchenko's previous startup, My Dropbox, a plagiarism detection service.
Initially programmed as a service to help students with their grammar and spelling, Grammarly claims it is used by over 30 million people and 70,000 professional teams today.
In November 2021, Grammarly raised $200 million at a $13 billion valuation from such investors as Baillie Gifford and BlackRock.
Forbes estimates that Lytvyn owns a 23% stake, which the company disputes, and that Grammarly is worth around $8 billion today.
forbes_facts: Lytvyn was born and raised in Ukraine and later obtained Canadian citizenship.

name: Gwynne Shotwell
sec_insider_companies: SPACE EXPLORATION TECHNOLOGIES CORP (SPCX) - President and COO; Polaris Inc. (PII) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Gwynne Shotwell is SpaceX's president and COO, and manages the operations of the commercial space exploration company founded by Elon Musk.
It's grown from a futuristic idea of enabling people to live on other planets to a company with over 13,000 employees and a valuation of $1.25 trillion.
In February 2026, SpaceX merged with another Musk-founded company, xAI, with plans to build giant AI data centers in orbit.
Shotwell was the 11th employee of SpaceX, joining the company in 2002. Before that, she was at spacecraft developer Microcosm as its space systems director.
Shotwell owns an estimated stake in SpaceX of 0.11%.
forbes_facts: NASA has selected SpaceX to be one of the companies that will transport astronauts to the Moon's surface as part of the Artemis IV program planned for 2028.

name: Kenny Troutt
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Kenny Troutt founded long-distance phone company Excel Communications in 1988 and took the company public in 1996.
In 1998, Troutt sold Excel Communications to Teleglobe in a $3.5 billion deal and reinvested the profits in stocks, bonds and horses.
An avid horse racing fan, Troutt owns WinStar Farm in Versailles, Kentucky, breeder of Thoroughbreds including a Kentucky Derby winner.
The son of a single mother who worked as a bartender, Troutt grew up in public housing in Mount Vernon, IL.
forbes_facts: For years, Troutt sponsored his sons' nationally competitive basketball teams, providing jerseys, equipment and even rides on his private jet to tournaments.

Vladimir Fartushyak himself wholly owns Zolla, another fast-fashion chain in Russia.

name: Alan Gerry
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Alan Gerry started building a cable TV network in upstate New York in 1956.
It became Cablevision Industries, which at its peak had 64 cable systems in 18 states.
Gerry sold Cablevision Industries to Time Warner in 1996 for a reported $2.7 billion; he pocketed an estimated $900 million.
He used that money to start own venture capital firm, Granite Associates, in 1996 to invest in emerging communications technologies.
forbes_facts: Gerry bought the site of the 1969 Woodstock festival and a decade later turned the location into the Bethel Woods Center for the Arts, an 800-acre cultural center
Gerry initially got into cable to increase demand for TV sets--he owned a television repair shop.

name: Rajeev Gulati
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun India (2019)
forbes_bio: Third generation scion Rajeev Gulati runs Delhi-based spice manufacturer MDH, which makes a range of Indian spices, including curry powders.
Gulati became chairman after the death of his father Dharampal Gulati, who was the face of brand appearing on all the packs and in TV commercials.
MDH has a factory in Sharjah to supply to the Middle Eastern market.
The business was founded by Gulati's grandfather in 1919 as Mahashian Di Hatti, a Punjabi phrase that translates into gentleman's shop.
forbes_facts: MDH's flagship product is Kitchen King, a mix of different spices.
In 2024, Hong Kong recalled specific MDH products saying they contained an excessive amount of ethylene oxide, a carcinogen. But tests by India's food regulator.

name: Petro Poroshenko
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2016); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Petro Poroshenko served as the president of Ukraine from 2014 to 2019, but made his fortune as Ukraine's "chocolate king."
Poroshenko got his start selling cocoa beans, then purchased several confectionery plants, uniting them under the company Roshen in 1995.
Roshen sells an estimated $800 million worth of chocolates, caramel, wafers, cakes and other confections across 35 countries.
His net worth fell by more than half after Russia invaded Ukraine as his confectionery firm Roshen was forced to shut two factories in Kyiv and nearby Boryspil.
